topics.title: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the Cartesian sign convention to distances and heights for mirrors and lenses.
Relate the focal length of a spherical mirror to its radius of curvature for paraxial rays.
Use the mirror equation and magnification to locate and describe images formed by spherical mirrors.
Apply Snell's law and the properties of relative refractive index to the bending of light.
Explain lateral shift in a glass slab and calculate the apparent depth of an object under a liquid.

topics.title: Total internal reflection and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: State the conditions for total internal reflection and relate the critical angle to refractive index.
Explain how totally reflecting prisms and optical fibres use total internal reflection.

topics.title: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses

concepts.learning_objective: Use the relation for refraction at a single spherical surface between two media.
Use the lens maker's formula to relate focal length to radii of curvature and refractive index.
Apply the thin lens formula and magnification to locate and describe images formed by lenses.

topics.title: Power of a lens and combination of thin lenses

concepts.learning_objective: Define the power of a lens in dioptres and relate its sign to the type of lens.
Find the effective power, focal length and magnification of thin lenses in contact.
Relate the angle of deviation of a prism to the angles of incidence, emergence and the prism angle.
Use the minimum deviation condition to find the refractive index of a prism, including a thin prism.
Explain how a simple microscope magnifies and calculate its magnifying power.
Describe image formation in a compound microscope and calculate its magnifying power.
Calculate the magnifying power and tube length of a refracting telescope in normal adjustment.
Evaluate how objective size and mirror objectives improve light gathering, resolution and image quality.
